reason: The text demonstrates multiple instances of non-leaders exercising significant agency. The Hebrew midwives Shiprah and Puah actively defy Pharaoh's command to kill Hebrew infants, choosing to fear God instead (וַתִּירֶאן הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִים וְלֹא עָשׂוּ). Moses' mother makes strategic decisions to hide and then place her child in the river (וַתִּצְפְּנֵהוּ...וַתִּקַּח לוֹ תֵּבַת). Moses' sister takes initiative to approach Pharaoh's daughter (וַתֹּאמֶר אֲחֹתוֹ). Pharaoh's daughter exercises moral agency through compassion and the decision to adopt the child (וַתַּחְמֹל עָלָיו). These figures are not leaders, yet they each make consequential choices that drive the narrative forward.
